summary: The note reports that Voyager 2 crossed the termination shock on August 30, 2007, and then entered the heliosheath. It states that this crossing occurred about 1 billion miles (1.6 billion km) closer to the Sun than where Voyager 1 made its crossing. The note attributes the difference to the interstellar magnetic field and says the southern hemisphere of the heliosphere is being pushed inward.
one_line: Voyager 2 crossed the termination shock and entered the heliosheath on August 30, 2007, closer to the Sun than Voyager 1.
key_facts: On August 30, 2007, Voyager 2 passed the termination shock.
After passing the termination shock, Voyager 2 entered the heliosheath.
Voyager 2 entered the heliosheath approximately 1 billion miles (1.6 billion km) closer to the Sun than Voyager 1 did.
The note attributes the difference in crossing distance to the interstellar magnetic field of deep space.
The southern hemisphere of the Solar System's heliosphere is being pushed in.
